name: Dom zu St. Jakob Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The baroque Cathedral of St. James in Innsbruck impresses with magnificent ceiling frescoes by the Asam brothers, the revered Cranach Mariahilf painting, and festive organ chimes.
beschreibung:
Overview

The imposing Innsbruck Cathedral of St. James (Dom zu St. Jakob) serves as the episcopal seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Innsbruck and stands as one of the most significant baroque ecclesiastical monuments in the entire Alpine region. Erected upon the foundations of an earlier medieval house of worship, the present magnificent cathedral was constructed between 1717 and 1724 following master designs by the renowned baroque architect Johann Jakob Herkomer. The distinctive twin-tower facade of pale limestone defines the skyline of the historic old town, forming a majestic contrast against the rugged limestone pinnacles of the Nordkette mountain range. As an enduring spiritual center and landmark on the Tyrolean Way of Saint James, the cathedral captivates worshipers, art connoisseurs, and international travelers alike.

Route & Requirements

From the world-famous Golden Roof in the heart of Innsbruck's historic core, a brief two-minute stroll through the narrow, cobbled Pfarrgasse brings visitors directly before the spacious portals of the cathedral. The bright, light-filled interior astounds guests with its festive baroque harmony: masterful ceiling frescoes by the acclaimed Bavarian brothers Cosmas Damian and Egid Quirin Asam depict the life and miracles of Saint James in brilliant illusionistic perspective. The internationally revered high-altar painting Mariahilf by Lucas Cranach the Elder ranks among the most celebrated Marian icons in Christian art history. Another highlight is the opulent bronze tomb of Archduke Maximilian III by sculptor Caspar Gras. The cathedral interior is barrier-free, level, and demands no physical exertion.

Visit & Arrival

The cathedral welcomes visitors daily from 07:30 to 18:30 with free admission for sightseeing and contemplative prayer, outside of scheduled liturgical masses, festive concerts, or weddings. Arrival by public transportation: from Innsbruck Main Railway Station, a level ten-minute walk through the pedestrian streets leads straight to Domplatz. Alternatively, numerous city bus and tram lines stop nearby at Maria-Theresien-Straße or Marktplatz. Motorists can utilize the centrally located underground parking garages Altstadtgarage, Marktplatzgarage, or Congressgarage, all situated within easy walking distance of the historic pedestrian zone.

Tips

Daily at precisely 12:10 noon, the monumental Innsbruck Cathedral Chimes ring out with the celebrated Mariahilf carillon, echoing far across the rooftops of the old town. Combine your cathedral visit with a cultural tour of the adjacent Imperial Hofburg Palace, a view of the Court Church, and a relaxing walk beneath the ancient shade trees of the surrounding Hofgarten gardens.
preis: Free admission (donations toward the conservation of the baroque episcopal church appreciated)
